rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Good afternoon.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: I'd like to welcome Members back to this meeting of the Culture, Communications, Welsh Language, Sport and International Relations Committee.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: We'll now move to an evidence session with S4C regarding allegations concerning bullying at the channel.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: I'll ask our witnesses to introduce themselves for the record.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I'm Rhodri Williams, chair of S4C.

rows.speaker: Chris Jones
rows.text: Chris Jones, non-executive member of the S4C board.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: I'll ask whether any Members have any declarations of interest.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Could I just put on record—?

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: It's not an interest in terms of Standing Orders, but I do think I should place on the public record that I used to be a member of the management team at S4C and I know both witnesses before us this afternoon.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you, Alun.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: This session has been rearranged from 14 December last year following the unexpected and unfortunate illness of the former chief executive, Sian Doyle.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: We all wish her a speedy recovery, of course.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Before we start today, I'd like to put on record how concerning recent events have been.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: While S4C is a matter reserved to the UK Government, it is a unique organisation.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Every one of us has a personal interest in the channel's success.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: The channel's work over the last four decades in providing Welsh language content is something that we can all be proud of.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: S4C also has an important role to play in assisting to deliver the aim of ensuring a million Welsh speakers by 2050.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: However, as you will be aware, the seriousness of the recent situation has undermined the channel's reputation.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: This is a cause for concern for us all.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Our session today will focus on the organisational response following the report on the working environment and atmosphere at S4C, as well as questions on S4C's governance arrangements.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: I don't need to say how important it is that you restore the confidence of those who work in S4C, as well as with S4C, and the people of Wales who rely on S4C content.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: S4C should be a channel that provides high-quality, unique and independent public broadcasting to the people of Wales.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: You have a responsibility to repair the recent damage caused.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Our hope is that we can get to the root of some of these issues in our session today and start the process of rebuilding our national broadcaster.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: I'd like to warn viewers watching today that this session's proceedings could include themes that could cause distress for some people.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: So, if you're happy, we'll go straight into questions.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: What do you think S4C has done to restore stability in your organisation since the Capital Law report was published?

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: And what are the next steps you'll be taking?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The first thing that's happened, in terms of providing stability, is that we've put interim arrangements in place where the duties and responsibilities of the chief executive and chief content officer are shared by Elin Morris, the chief operating officer, and Geraint Evans, the director of content and publication strategy.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: That has given us some stability and it has succeeded in making our staff—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And for me, and I'd like to emphasise this point at the very outset, the priority here, and what is central to this whole question, is the well-being and safety of our staff, and they have responded positively to those new arrangements.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: They understand, of course, that they are interim arrangements.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: In due course, we will need to appoint a permanent, full-time chief executive, and then, perhaps, it will be a matter for the chief executive, in consultation with the board, to decide on the shape of the management team.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It doesn't necessarily mean that we will fill those roles that existed in the previous regime.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I was very pleased, as you can imagine, to see among the committee's papers for today that you had received a response from BECTU that confirms what I am saying. It's not my reflection on the fact that staff are now happier—BECTU confirm that.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: As I understand it, they've had two meetings with staff members within S4C, one in December and one Friday of last week, and the response has been positive.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, that's the first step, if you like.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The next step, and perhaps we will come to this in due course, is to look at what needs to be—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I would agree 100 per cent with your comments, Chair, that we do need to rebuild confidence in the organisation, because from the moment we received that first letter, as non-executive members of the board, on 28 April of last year, raising these concerns—not raising them with S4C for the first time but raising them with us as non-executive members for the first time—I do think that a great deal of damage was done to the reputation of the organisation, to the confidence of the organisation and to the self-respect of many people.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It has been the most difficult period in the history of S4C, I would think.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, as part of that process—and again, I'd like to refer to the BECTU letter, where they make suggestions—we are eager to work with them and with our staff in order to do what is necessary to restore that confidence.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I would place it into four headings, and those are leadership—and that relates clearly to the appointment of a new chief executive; culture—the creation of a culture where people can feel safe at work and where they do not live in fear; that the current policies are in place and that those policies are fit to safeguard staff and do provide ways and means of dealing with concerns that arise; and finally in terms of governance: are there issues around the model of governance currently in place that need to be reviewed or looked at anew?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We will need to do all of that during the coming months.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you for that.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: We'll move on to Carolyn Thomas.

rows.speaker: Carolyn Thomas
rows.text: Good afternoon.

rows.speaker: Carolyn Thomas
rows.text: I will be asking my questions in English.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: If it's okay, I'll continue to answer in Welsh.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The board is meeting next a fortnight today, as it happens, and in that meeting we will be discussing a package of measures under those headings.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Some of the work, as you would expect, has already begun.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: By then, officials will have been looking at some of the issues that I've already referred to and will be bringing recommendations to that meeting, and we will put processes in place for that reviewing that needs to be done, and a wider discussion.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Because in terms of having policies such as those relating to whistleblowing, respect in the workplace, discipline, complaints, we have policies on those issues already.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We will need to review those.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But what Capital Law's report tells us is that it wasn't a problem with our policies that was causing the difficulties within S4C and the concerns among members of staff; the culture and the leadership of S4C was creating those problems.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The report is very clear on that.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I don't want to speak too much about questions that we dealt with yesterday, but there is a danger, I think, that people aren't willing to accept the truth about what's happened here, and that what is in the report on the welfare of staff and our duty of care towards staff is somewhat ignored completely.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I would want to emphasise there that the evidence we received in the Capital Law report shows clearly that there is a need for a culture where people can be safe, where they can express doubts and criticism without fear of consequences.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: That process of changing culture is key to our success as an organisation in the future.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Of course, that includes us as a board—I wouldn't want to disregard our role in providing that example in that context.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It also includes the leadership and staff.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But I do believe that, for that to be successful, I would foresee that there's a need for external support.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I mentioned governance arrangements and our standing orders, which set out how the body works, and I think that, with that also, we would want to hear other people's views regarding our standing orders, not that we decide, 'Oh, this needs to be changed, this is what we're going to do', and that's the end of it.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I think we would want to consult widely and look at good practice in other places, and to see if there are lessons that we can learn from other places.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Carolyn, before we come back, Llyr just wants to ask a question.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Certainly.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We have spoken to BECTU—with their full-time representative in Cardiff, as well as their representative within the S4C workforce—and they have been very happy to collaborate with us.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: One of the first things we did when this process started—Chris and myself were involved in the meeting, with one other non-executive member of the board—was to speak to BECTU regarding what needed to be done at the outset.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And of course, in that discussion with BECTU, that's where we agreed that the only way in which this process could work effectively was if we had in place a mechanism that allowed staff members to speak openly without fear of consequences as a result of the comments that they would make.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, we have co-operated with BECTU in the past.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Carwyn Donovan, as is clear in his letter to you, Chair, makes it clear that BECTU have suggestions to make as to how we can work together to ensure that we don't see these kinds of problems arising again.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And we will most certainly be doing that in moving to the future.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It's not in place as of yet.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: As I say, the board will meet in a fortnight's time, and the intention at that time would be to put those arrangements in place.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Llyr.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: Thank you.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: It's been very useful that you have scoped out those four areas, if you like, or the themes that you'll be focusing on—leadership, culture, policies and governance.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: Of course, in presenting those elements, when you were talking about leadership, you referred to a chief executive and perhaps the executive directors.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: But of course, you have a leadership responsibility too in that context.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: So, when you said there was a discussion going to be in the board on these issues, do you expect there'll be a discussion on your role as chair?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I would expect us to discuss all of our roles.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Clearly, a chair and a board have an important role in setting standards and ensuring that standards are adhered to, and in demonstrating those values and standards that we want to see within the organisation in the way that we ourselves conduct ourselves, and to place an emphasis on the kinds of values that we expect the organisation to act in accordance with.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: Because in the way that you presented that context earlier, I just felt that there was a suggestion, and perhaps it could be heard yesterday in the evidence, that this responsibility is for others and other people have to deal with this.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: Now, that is true to some extent—of course it is—but at the end of the day, you are the chair, and people's perception would be, fair or not, that the buck stops there with you.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: How would you describe your performance over this last period?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: If I could say a few words first of all on where responsibility lies.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Of course, at the end of the day, the buck stops with the chair.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: May I say quite clearly here that I fully accept responsibility for the decisions that have been made by the board, and that they were unanimous decisions by the board?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I wouldn't want to suggest for a second that I would turn my back on those responsibilities.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I am quite convinced that we as a board had made the right decisions at the right time.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: More importantly—the crucial thing for me—I am entirely confident that we did the right thing for those individuals within S4C, and some outside S4C, who have suffered under the previous leadership.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: In terms of how that formal responsibility is divided, we are there to set expectations.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: In relation to policies, the board is responsible for strategy, the executive is responsible for executing that strategy.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The contract of the chief executive says that it's the responsibility of the chief executive to ensure that S4C has a working environment where everyone treats each other with respect, and where dignity and fairness are at the core of all of the company's activities.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: If you place that paragraph alongside the Capital Law report, then it is clear that that was not happening.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: But are you disappointed that you hadn't picked up on that earlier—I'm sure you are—and do you acknowledge that that perhaps is a failure?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Certainly, I'm sorry that we didn't pick up on it earlier, but I don't think that you can place blame on people for not realising that.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Because BECTU wrote to the chief executive first of all on 2 December 2022, and BECTU—just as they have offered to help in the process of making improvements now—did offer the chief executive at that time that they would work with her to deal with the problems.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We as a board received reports from the chief executive on that process.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We received those through the people and remuneration committee, which is responsible for HR issues, and we received them directly as members of the board.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: What we were told was that steps were being put in place, that there was a listening exercise with staff, and that everything was moving in the right direction.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, yes, I am frustrated that we hadn't understood the gravity of the problems earlier and the concerns that staff members had, but on the other hand, there was no evidence.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We received some evidence when we met in Caernarfon in January 2023 that there was some disquiet, as I would describe it.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But my interpretation of that was that S4C staff in Caernarfon particularly felt that they were being forgotten, that they were out of the picture, not the kind of serious allegations that were raised by BECTU later on.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: I want to go back to that, if I may, Rhodri.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Rhodri and Chris, both of you have been clear in your evidence this afternoon that the first time you heard about the staff experiences and the problems within the organisation was in April of last year.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: I think that I remember reports that Gwyn Williams had discussed this with you in June 2022, and that there had been reports to you as members of the board at that time.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: You're smiling, so have I misunderstood, perhaps?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I am trying to work out in my head how to deal with the point that you've raised in an appropriate manner.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: If I say that there was a process related to HR that was happening at that time, and an appeal was made in relation to that process, and it was heard by the chair of the people and remuneration committee.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: That appeal was rejected.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: That was the only involvement that I am aware of from that time.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I don't have any record—none of us have a record—of any complaints being raised at that point in relation to the internal culture and the behaviour of senior officials.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I don't believe that we had evidence of that until BECTU wrote to us.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The closest we came was, I would say, within the week or 10 days prior to BECTU's letter arriving, I certainly heard from a number of individuals working within the sector that there was a problem and that there was disquiet among staff, but none of that had been reported to us.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Now, perhaps, under a different system where people would be working in the office five days a week and where committee meetings, as well as board meetings, would be happening within one of S4C's offices, there may be more opportunity for chats off the record.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It was certainly something that I was familiar with when I worked for Ofcom many years ago, where we would go to the headquarters in London to work and we would meet the chair, the chief executive and other members of the board, and we'd have chats.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: They'd ask, 'How are things going in Wales?', and you'd have the opportunity to do that.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But the opportunities to do those things are much reduced now, and one of the things that we need to look at for the future, perhaps, is whether we need to adapt our arrangements, so that we create more opportunities for somebody to come to us over a cup of coffee and say, 'Can I have a quiet word about this?'

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But that didn't happen until we—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And if you look at the BECTU letter, Carwyn Donovan uses the words 'out of the blue', so he certainly didn't expect us to be aware of these problems.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: The problem I have with that is that Capital Law's report suggests and says something quite different.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: I'll read one part of it to you:

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: That's the workforce you were responsible for, and you didn't know anything about it.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: No, and—

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: I find that quite incredible, because you are an experienced manager.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But not operating in this context as a manager.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: In other words, I'd go to an office—

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: You have decades of experience in this area, Rhodri.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Decades of experience.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: You are an experienced chairperson, and you didn't know until you received a letter from the union what was happening within the organisation where you were chair.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: No. None of—

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Really?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: —the staff had approached me until that time.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And there's a reason for that, Alun.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I think it's clear in the BECTU letter why that hadn't happened.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The reason it hadn't happened was that nobody had felt that they could approach me or another member of the board because of fear of the chief executive.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The behaviour of the chief executive and the conduct of the chief executive, and, again, it's described very clearly in the Capital Law report, isn't it?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The conduct and behaviour of the chief executive was full of conflict, abusive and didn't take account of people's needs.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: People were scared—

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: I'd just like to remind people that if we are discussing certain people, they're not here to respond, so we'd like to focus on governance and not individuals.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: But the question, Rhodri, is that you were responsible for her and her behaviour and her work.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: You were responsible for it.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But if one isn't aware—that is, again, what I would say to that, Alun, is that once we learnt of the gravity of these complaints, a meeting of the board was held on that same day.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We agreed that day that we would establish an external inquiry so that people could talk—that is, because the letter said that the reason that no complaints had been received was because of fear, we decided that we needed to create this mechanism, this safe space, where people could express their concerns without having to worry about other people's attitudes.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We took action very swiftly after that to put that process in place.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It was Friday when we received the letter, the Monday was a bank holiday, by the Tuesday, Capital Law had been appointed.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you for that.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Tom wants to come in, then we'll go back to Llyr.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, there are processes in place.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The board, as we've been describing, has a committee that's responsible for these matters.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We have officials who are part of a management team that report regularly.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, for example, on 22 December, I received an e-mail from the chief executive saying that a meeting had been held with BECTU, that it had been a successful one.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The meeting had begun with Carwyn Donovan saying he was reassured because of the speed of our response, and it was agreed to work closer with BECTU.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, I think it is reasonable for us to believe what was being said.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Now, it's possible that that assessment was not as good as it was, but from the information available to us as members of the board, I think we did really think that steps had been put in place—this listening exercise had happened—and that the problems that had been outlined and discussed with BECTU were improving.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: There was no reason for us to think that that wasn't true, and I'm not sure what other sources we could have had—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Certainly, staff members would have had an opportunity to speak with me, to speak with other members of the board, but if they didn't feel comfortable, if they didn't feel safe in raising those issues, then it wasn't possible, and that is the great sadness, because I think, the point that has been made by Alun, the staff had suffered significantly during those months, and that is of great concern to me personally and as chair of the board.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Could I just say one other thing?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: In taking your comments into account, Chair, may I encourage you to look again at the Capital Law report?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: That makes it clear why people hadn't spoken out—they feared speaking out.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: There was a culture of fear.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It says in the report that that had been expressed as a deliberate policy of creating fear because that's what was needed to secure culture change.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Yes, but we can't create that confidence if they live in a culture of fear and threat, which was the case.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I mean, there was a whistle-blowing policy—I don't think that that's necessarily the policy that should have been used.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: There's a dignity at work policy—someone could have raised questions on that, that it wasn't being implemented effectively. There's a discipline policy, a complaints procedure.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Don't think that I think everything's perfect—I'm not suggesting that for one moment—but those opportunities did exist.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But what the Capital Law report says—what the staff themselves say—is that they lived in fear, and that's why—

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: I'm going go over to Alun for a supplementary question, but I'm aware that we only have 20 minutes left from the time allocated.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Would you have time, after 2 o'clock, to stay with us for about an extra quarter of an hour, if required?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Yes, of course.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you for that.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: But I'm still aware of time, so, Alun, if you could be brief.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: And that's what causes concern for me.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: You've described—.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: And I don't think anyone denies your evidence this afternoon, Rhodri, about the atmosphere in S4C.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: You were the chair and you didn't know anything about it.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: And we have to ask the question then: where were you?

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Where were you when staff members at S4C felt too frightened to speak about their experiences in work and the chair wasn't there?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, it's not a matter of my not being there—

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Well, where were you?

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Why didn't you realise?

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: If the situation was as bad as you've described to us this afternoon, why didn't you realise what was happening?

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: That's what I don't understand.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, because somebody would have to tell us.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Now, I've—

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Surely you would have known how—.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Come on.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I've spent long enough in our offices in the Egin and in Central Square, less, I have to say, in the Caernarfon office, and during that time there were opportunities.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I know many of the staff well enough and have spoken to them informally, outside of meetings, but nobody expressed these concerns.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It was only after the BECTU letter arrived that the floodgates opened.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: After that point, I received text messages, I received phone calls, I had face-to-face meetings with members of staff.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But it was only then—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The opportunities existed, I was there before then, but it was only after that letter was received that I received those reports from members of staff.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: And you had reports from staff directly.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Yes.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Face to face.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Yes.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Okay.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Okay.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: We'll move on to Llyr.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: Thank you.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: How did you, as chair, and how did the board, perhaps, consider the impact of publishing the report on the individuals named in Capital Law's report?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, as I said at the outset, the people who have been impacted most by this process are S4C staff.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: I don't deny that, but that wasn't my question.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: No, no, but it was they who were central to the whole process.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: This question of creating a safe space, of ensuring that—

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: Yes, I understand all of that.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: —all conversations centred on the staff.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Now, we told the staff that others would not see the report before they did.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I don't think it would have been reasonable or fair for anyone, whatever reference is made to them in the report, to have access to that report before the staff themselves saw it.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And, given what was happening and the campaign that was going on in the press against me, against the board, against S4C, against DCMS, against the Secretary of State, would it have been responsible for us to provide that report beforehand to people who would have an opportunity to misuse it and to further—plenty of efforts had been made already, but to further attempt to undermine the content of the report?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: That has happened since then.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It's being denied that any of this happened.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Despite the weight of evidence that we have received, it's suggested that there is no truth in it at all.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, the report demonstrates clearly to us that the concerns expressed by BECTU have been borne out.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: That is, BECTU's description of the culture of fear was very accurate indeed.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And therefore I have no reason to believe that we have treated anybody unfairly.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: To be honest, it would have been entirely unfair for the staff if they'd heard that people who were no longer employed by S4C had seen the report before they had.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: But there is a process of informing people that it's about to be published, not necessarily sharing a copy.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: Do you think on a human level or on a moral level, or from a courtesy perspective, that people should have some sort of notice that it was about to be published?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Our focus was on ensuring that the staff received the information before anybody else—

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: Well, yes, of course, receiving the information.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: —and that's what our focus has been throughout—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And because of the nature of the report, it wasn't known.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We didn't say beforehand, 'This will be published in seven days' time or whatever'.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It was very tight in terms of timescale between the time that we were ready to publish and that process of sharing the report with staff and explaining to them, and giving them an opportunity to ask us questions on the next steps.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And I have no concerns about not having shared it with anybody else.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: No, but in terms of informing people that a report was about to be published, you would expect that somebody who's named would at least have an opportunity, 24 hours or a few hours, just to prepare themselves that something was being published that talks about them.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: I'm just getting that you're being somewhat rash and very hard-hearted in that regard.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: I'm not talking about sharing a copy of the report, but in terms of a moral responsibility to individuals, don't you feel any sort of responsibility in that regard?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I feel a moral responsibility towards the staff.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: So, once somebody leaves S4C, that's it, is it?

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: If they're former staff, you're not part of—?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: No, we're talking here about people, about two individuals who had been dismissed, and, as I've said, were waging a very public campaign, using—

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: Well, if you want to frame it as one group against another, but you're sharp enough to know that perhaps not informing somebody beforehand would give them something to throw back at you, if that's the game you're playing.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, I can understand that point, but in the discussions between ourselves and our legal team, the decision was taken not to do that.

rows.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
rows.text: Thank you.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Okay.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: We'll go on to Alun Davies now.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: If I could just say one other thing on that issue.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: When—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We have discussed these issues with DCMS officials since the receipt of the first BECTU letter, and made them aware of that, and we do speak regularly.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Yes, clearly.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: On more than one occasion during this period, I have asked the official that we deal with whether it would be beneficial to arrange a face-to-face meeting, or a virtual meeting if it came to that, with the Secretary of State, and the response I was given was that that was not necessary.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: I find that completely shocking—shocking.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: For someone who actually thinks that broadcasting shouldn't be devolved, that isn't something I would have wanted to hear.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: It reflects great problems with the DCMS, I think.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: But I was going to ask another question to Chris, if I may.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: During the discussions that you've been having as a board and as non-execs during this period, did you ask for support from the DCMS, the BBC, or Welsh Government, from any one of those governmental organisations?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Perhaps it would be easier for me to answer that, Chris.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, we did have discussions with the DCMS and Welsh Government to ensure that they were aware of the procedural issues, and I'd like to emphasise that: there was no question of sharing any findings or the results of the report, and that wouldn't have been possible because we didn't know until the team within Capital Law presented their report to us.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And, on all occasions, the response—and more specifically from DCMS than anywhere else—was that this was an operational issue for the S4C board, and it wasn't their place to advise.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Yes, yes.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: But I had a slightly different question, with a different emphasis, to Chris: had you asked for support while you were considering—because I take it, as non-execs, you were discussing amongst yourselves what was happening, and there were reports in the media; it would have been odd if you weren't talking to each other—had you asked for external support to help you deal with these issues?

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Okay.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Thank you for that.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Rhodri, if I could just end on this: you will have seen reports from the select committee after your appearance yesterday.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: They have said there's a need for new leadership at S4C.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: When, I think, Steve Crabb, asked you whether you were going to seek reappointment in April, you gave quite an odd answer, in my opinion, that you would be happy to accept reappointment.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: You didn't say that you were going to apply for that; you said that you would be happy to accept a reappointment.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: I thought that was an odd way of wording things.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Have you considered, overnight, your position and where you stand today after hearing the views of the select committee?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Yes, of course, and I have discussed with others what happened yesterday.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: What surprised me in our discussion yesterday wasn't this element that the committee wasn't eager to see me reappointed, but the emphasis being solely on process and the end of this process.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: There was no focus whatsoever yesterday on what staff members in S4C have suffered.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: There was no concern expressed about what they have had to go through over a long period of months.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: My concern is that—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Many people have commented on what should happen.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I don't doubt their motivation at all, but anything that creates further instability for our staff is not going to help the staff and it's not going to help the organisation as a whole either.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: That's why, if the Secretary of State were to ask me—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And that is the process—there's no question of making an application.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: There is no application process, as such; it's a matter for the Secretary of State to reappoint a chair or members of bodies, and it is very clear too in the rules and regulations.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And as you kindly referred to earlier, I've been around long enough to know that one should never take it for granted that there will be a reappointment, and that's why I had used the wording that I did.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: I understand that.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Rhodri, you were arrested in campaigning for S4C, weren't you?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: A number of times.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: A number of times.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Your commitment to S4C has been lifelong.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: I understand that and I don't question that.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: But the issues we've seen over the last few years have been very difficult, and I understand that.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: But what I'm saying is, when you're talking about the suffering of staff members at S4C, you were part of the leadership that caused that.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: And you said earlier that 'the buck stops'.

rows.speaker: Alun Davies
rows.text: Don't you feel that you have a responsibility to consider things further?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: There is always a responsibility on a chair or a non-executive member of any body, of course that's the case, and that is ongoing from the day of appointment up until the end of your period of service.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: As I said at the outset, my emphasis and my interest through this whole process was and remains today on the well-being of the staff.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Not a word has been expressed to me that any member of the current S4C staff believes that it would be beneficial for S4C if I were to resign today.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Not one of the production companies that I've been involved with or have had discussions with during this period have suggested that it would be beneficial.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: To be honest, the message is quite clear that what they want to see happening is a period of stability, allowing the process of improvement, which is already in play, as I made clear earlier—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Within S4C, the working environment has improved significantly since the departure of two senior officials, and what we need now is stability to allow that process to continue to work.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Okay, thank you for that.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: We'll move finally to Tom.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Okay, we'll go to Hefin and then Tom.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Hefin.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: What I would say is that difficulties of this kind in so many organisations and bodies in Wales have been too common during this recent period.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The rugby union is only one body that has dealt with different problems.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: What I would say is that the circumstances in every case are different, and that the responses have always been different.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I don't know enough about the situation in the rugby union to know enough about it to be able to provide a view.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: What I've said already sets out my views with regards to S4C and what should happen in S4C, and my conclusion in that regard would be that for me to resign today, or at any other time before the end of my term, would not be of any benefit to S4C.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I can imagine that it would make other people feel happy and self-satisfied, but, if you speak to our staff or with our providers, our partners, the response is different, and some of them have expressed that.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I see that—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: There's a letter from a production company that has been sent to the committee expressing that view.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The chair of one of the most successful independent television companies in Wales in a radio interview this morning expressed the same view.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Under those circumstances, I am completely at peace that I am doing the right thing.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Okay.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: We'll move on to Tom.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: As Chris suggested earlier, the information provided to us wasn't sufficiently consistent and detailed to allow us to identify any difficulties here.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: We have changed that system during the period in which Capital Law undertook their work, so that the dashboard that is now provided regularly—four times a year—to the people and remuneration committee does identify those patterns.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And what it shows is that, during the year 2023, almost twice as many people left S4C than had done in the two years previous to that.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, steps have been taken already.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I would accept fully that we need to improve those processes.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Just as we have a dashboard that demonstrates how many people are using Clic, and how many people are using iPlayer, we should also be receiving that information.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, not routinely, no. It did emerge and because this process had taken a long period of time between the end of April and November, there was internal discussion on these issues that was ongoing, and a decision was taken that we needed to improve processes, and, of course, there was a staff survey conducted during that period, and that staff survey told us what would emerge in due time in the Capital Law report—that there was a high level of dissatisfaction with the leadership.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: No, not until we received BECTU's letter.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Following BECTU's letter—

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It varies over a period of time.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: In terms of absences from work, there was an increase during this period.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I can't, off the top of my head, say whether that had started in 2023, before April, or whether it was from April onwards.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And that's why we had to make sure we had better data, and that we received it more regularly.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It's something that's been a topic of discussion in the board, to ensure that that matrix of measurements is available, and that they are available regularly.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I think that is the point—you have to have them regularly enough to see whether the changes are significant.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But, again, there was nothing before BECTU's letter arrived that made us feel that there was something wrong.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, it wasn't good enough, certainly, because if it was, we would have been aware that there was something wrong here.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But it wasn't, and that's why it has been changed.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: That's why there is a new process in place now that does provide that information.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The one thing that I would say is that we weren't hearing from one source only that improvements were happening, or that the complaints that had been presented by BECTU were being dealt with, and that things were improving.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It wasn't just the chief executive that was saying that, but there's an human resources director, and there are other members of the management team.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, it wasn't just coming from one source.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But as I say, I would have been delighted if we'd had some early warning system that would allow us to say, 'We need to do more', but there wasn't one.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: No, I don't think—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: There were a number of weaknesses, I think, that came out during our discussions.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: One was a very low level of performance assessment with staff.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: During the last year, the performance of the management team wasn't assessed.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: None of them was assessed for over a year.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, those interviews wouldn't happen with the chair or members of the board as people leave.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, no. That's not the case, as it happens.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Well, it didn't happen in this case, and, again, I know personally some of the staff members who did leave during that period.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: They did provide evidence to the Capital Law team, but they did not express those concerns when leaving.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And, of course, and, again, may I refer you back to the report, you will see comments from the chief executive on the number of people she wished to see leave the organisation.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I think it said that there were 50 staff that we'd be better off without.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, there was a deliberate attempt here made to see staff leave and that wasn't something that came to my attention until the report itself was received.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: And may I also say that, of course, any period of change—when you change how an organisation operates, then it's natural that there will be some churn in staff, that new blood will come in and that some staff will leave.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: There is nothing inherently wrong with that.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But there is a way of doing that, and that's what all this is about, I think.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It's the way of doing things.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: As it happens, I sit on the board of the Consumer Council for Water, and during the past three years, they've had a new chief executive, and they have led a process of internal change, but they've done so by taking the staff with them, by ensuring that the performance of the staff of the water consumer council, in their staff surveys, are almost irrationally high, because the focus has been entirely on the health, well-being and care of staff.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But that's not what happened with us.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Because, quite simply, the circumstances that led to the dismissal of the chief content officer occurred on a Saturday in Nantes, following a rugby match.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The chief executive had attended the same meetings—well, they weren't meetings—but the chief executive was present at the same locations where these events took place, which led to that decision.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, the chief executive had an interest in that issue.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: She hadn't shared that with anyone within S4C, although the wider industry in Wales all knew what had been said and to whom.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It was being reported in the press almost before we'd heard about these events.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, under those circumstances, and having receiving advice on procedure and on employment law and the appropriate steps to be taken, I took the decision that action had to be taken immediately in order to safeguard the reputation of S4C.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: As was mentioned earlier, I have been in this business for many years and have never come across a case of a senior official behaving in that way.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: If the new chief executive were to decide—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Of course, they will appoint somebody, whether that person will be a chief content officer or a director of content or a director of programming—there are all sorts of possible titles.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: When a new chief executive appoints, I would expect, as it happens, that the chair, whoever he or she may be, would be invited into that process.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I was involved in the process of appointing Llinos Griffin-Williams to S4C, because the post was one of those posts that carries the additional duties of being an executive director of the shadow unitary board.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Sorry, I don't know why I turned to English there.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The board will discuss that a fortnight today.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: In terms of how far we could go, I wouldn't think that an appointment would be made, if I'm perfectly honest, during the remainder of my term of office; I wouldn't expect it to happen within that period.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: We're very aware of how long you've stayed with us—thank you very much.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: I have two very brief questions, at the end.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: You mentioned to Alun, and this was raised yesterday, that you'd asked for many meetings with DCMS and that that hadn't happened.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Do you think it's appropriate, therefore, that it's the Secretary of State who has the powers in this situation if the Secretary of State doesn't show an interest in having a meeting?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I think that's beyond my responsibilities in terms of expressing a view on who should—.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: In other words, that's the framework that we're working within—

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: But perhaps the framework isn't working as well as it should at the moment.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: As I said, we have occasionally met with some Ministers from the department, but as I said, when I proposed that we should meet the Secretary of State to discuss this specific issue, as it happens, that offer was not accepted.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: It appears to me that when this process was ongoing, there wasn't a great deal of interest shown in it, but because of the way things have panned out—and that isn't how I would have imagined things developing when this whole process started—everyone, now, is taking an interest in all aspects of this.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: That's to be expected, isn't it?

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Just the final question: is there anything that you regret about the whole situation?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Yes.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I regret this point that we've been discussing that we as a board weren't aware of these concerns at an earlier stage.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I do regret, with hindsight, that the remit that we agreed with Capital Law was one that allowed the process to take a long period of time.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: There were reasons for that.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Because of this fear factor that I have referred to, that was a very important part of drawing up the remit in very broad terms that, of course, then allowed everyone to contribute to this process.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: So, in a way, we created a problem for ourselves.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: The BECTU complaint didn't refer to the board or to governance; it related to the management team, as it was referred to, although not every member of that management team was involved, but they couldn't be specific about complaints, and it wouldn't have been appropriate to name individuals in that scenario.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: BECTU had been very careful in that regard.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But, of course, that did mean that the process was lengthier and that the process did allow people who were the subjects of complaints to be contributing to it.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I do believe that it would have been more beneficial, perhaps, for our staff and for the mental health of our staff throughout this period, if we had agreed a remit that focused more on what BECTU were complaining about, rather than saying, 'Come to us to talk about anything that's on your mind.'

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But, with the information that we had at the time, I was quite content that we needed to put a process in place that was very open, in order to ensure that people had the confidence to contribute to it.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: But do I regret that now?

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Yes.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: We're very grateful for the additional time you've provided this afternoon.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: There will be a transcript of the meeting sent to you to ensure that it's a fair reflection of what's been said, and perhaps there will be some technical questions that we haven't been able to ask, and we'll want to write to you about those.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: But thank you very much for being with us this afternoon.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Thank you all very much for your time and for the way in which you have questioned us this afternoon.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: I have said in this committee previously that do we appreciate and are always willing to be held to account by you as elected Members.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Despite the fact that the circumstances are unpleasant, I am grateful for the way in which you have asked your questions and have dealt with us today.

rows.speaker: Rhodri Williams
rows.text: Thank you very much.

rows.speaker: Delyth Jewell
rows.text: Thank you very much.
